title: Co Rads and CT Severity Score in Covid 19 | CO Rads and CT Severity Score in Govid-19
description: The CO RADS classification denotes the suspicion of Covid-19 in a patient, ranging from CO-RADS-1, which is low suspicion, to CO-RADS-6, which is positive PCR in the patient. This is calculated by studies of the CTs of the lungs. The CT severity score is calculated by the average lung involvement of all 5 lobes, placed on a scale of 1-25, with 25 being full proper lung function. Though both are based on CT chest, their purpose is entirely different. CoRATS classification gives the level of suspicion of COVID pneumonia based on the CT findings,. Whereas CT severity score gives the extent of enolment in the lungs based on CT. To get into the classification, we will have to know the typical CT findings in COVID pneumonia. So these are the GGOs or ground glass opacities, crazy paving pattern and consolidation. GGOs or the ground glass opacities, these are hazy opacities,. But this opacity will not obscure underlying bronchial structures or pulmonary vessels. This is the typical glass which we see in windows or indoors so the purpose is to let light in but. The person on the other side will not be seen clearly i have this ground glass opacities. In the lungs so these are the ground glass opacities and this is the area of normal lung. So when we see the pulmonary vessels, the vascular markings can be seen. And this is the area of normal lung and this is the area of ground glass opacity. Next one is the crazy paving pattern. So this is nothing but ground glass opacity with superimposed intra and interlobular septal thickening. So what is crazy paving? So this we have commonly seen so this is a crazy paving so you have tiles of various sizes. And they are all placed together to give this appearance. Similarly we have this crazy paving. Appearance in the lungs in CT when we see this septa so the septa can be seen superimposed. On this area of ground glass opacity so that is crazy paving. Next is consolidation here the opacity will obscure underlying bronchial structures of. Pulmonary vessels and we can see air bronchograms so here we see this CT showing areas of patchy. Consolidation. We can have a look at this area of opacity but the. Underlying palantir vessels cannot be seen clearly so this is an area of. Consolidation and not a groundless opacity. You can also see in this area. Air bronchogram. Now we come to the CORADS classification. So when the CT findings are. Normal or you have non-infectious abnormalities like emphysema, we give a CORADS score of 1. And the level of suspicion is nil. When you have CT findings which are consistent with. Infections other than COVID-19 like low-bar pneumonia we say the level of. Suspicion is low and we give a CoRAT score of 2. When the CT findings are not. Clear and the COVID-19 cannot be ruled out we say it is indeterminate. Typically in cases of pulmonary edema where we have perihilar ground glass. We give a core at score of 3 in such a case. When the CT findings are present, suspicious for COVID-19 but not very typical, like we. Have groundless opacities but not subplural or which are unilateral, then you say the. Level of suspicion is high and we give the core at score of 4. When we have typical abnormalities like patchy ground glass opacities which are sub pleural,. Bilateral then we say these are typical findings, the level of suspicion is very high and we. Give Corat score of 5. There is a new addition 6 when the RT-PCR is already proven to be positive for the patient. So basically, CORATS 1 to 5 is based on CT scan findings. Next, we come to the CT severity score. Patients also directly telling about the score, CT severity score of 12 or 5 or 19 or 22. So first of all, we need to know what is the maximum score. So, the most commonly used CT severity score, we have seen a maximum score of 25. There is one more method by which people are calculating where the maximum score is 40. So, we need to first verify this. This is a semi-quantitative scoring. From 0 where there is no involvement or 25 maximum involvement. Basic anatomy, so two lungs, we have three lobes on right side and two lobes on the left. Side. We have a major fissure of the oblique fissure, a minor fissure of the horizontal fissure. On the right side. On the left side we have only a major fissure. So basically for the lobe identification we use the fissures. So these are the major fissures on both sides seen on axial section and on coronal section. But the minor fissure will be difficult to see on these sections. The sagittal section we can see this is a major fissure and this is a minor fissure. Lower lobe upper lobe middle lobe so this is essential for the calculation of. CT severity index so CT severity score how to calculate so for each lobe we. Calculate the scores and when the elongation element is absent we give 0 if it is. Less than 5% we give 1 5 to 25 we give 2 25 to 50 we give 3 50 to 75 we give 4 and. If it is more than 75 we give 5. Small CT chest we give 0 and then we scroll the images and for each lobe we try to find. Out the amount of lung involvement. If it is less than 5% now 1 and in this case it looks like 5 to 25% we give 2 but we need. To scroll and see the entire lobe and if there is doubt use coronal images and this is a. Case with severe lung involvement more than 75% so we give a score of 5 so this is done. For each lobe and then finally we add them all together so maximum score will be 5 x. That is 25. This is an example case where in every lobe we have patchy ground glass. Opacity is less than 5%. So on the right side three lobes and left side two lobes everywhere. It is less than 5% in each lobe. So for each lobe we give a score of 1 totaling 5 out of. Of a maximum score of 25. But one important thing we need to note here is that in each. Of these slopes, the environment is less than 5% and totally it may be less than 5%, but. The score is 5. So some people think that 5 out of 25 is 20% and say that overall lung. Enrollment is 20% which is wrong so we need to calculate for each loop and then. Give the score it may not correlate with the percentage of lung enrollment in. Total one more important thing is that the CT changes over time so early. Stage of pneumonia infection in COVID-19 that is 0 to 4 days we see ground glass. Opacities and partial crazy pavings. The progressive stage that is between 5 to 8. Days we see extension of ground glass opacities and increased crazy pavings. The peak. Stage is 10 to 13 days we can see consolidation and in the late stage the. Obsorption stage more than 14 days or two weeks. We see gradual resolution. Findings which can be seen in this stage or sublural bands or fibrosis. So the normal CT action section. So early infection can show. That she's a plural drone glass opacity. Which can. Extend to other areas and to the opposite side. Then we can have crazy paving pattern. Then we have areas of consolidation. And at the later stages we have this areas of sublural bands and some fibrosis. So usually we do serial image interpretation, we look at serial images of the chest, cranial. To caudal, look at every lobe, try to find the score of each lobe and then finally add. It. We also use this volume image interpretation so here we see this areas this light bluish areas. These are areas of covid infection you see patches on both sides so with volume image. Interpretation it is much easier to note the findings so the typical findings are groundless. Capacities which are sub plural that is peripheral and bilateral crazy paving. Pattern and concern then we saw about the square ads 1 to 5 and 6 square at 6. So we usually give a score like 5 out of 25 or 10 out of 25. So the maximum one should also be mentioned. And we also saw that the CT findings change. Your web time.
